name: GitHub MCP Server
purpose: Repo management, issues, PRs and codebase search from inside the coding agent
description: Gives the agent direct access to GitHub repos: read issues, review PRs, search the codebase, summarize commits, compare branches, explain GitHub Actions workflows. Presenter (VirtualizationHowto) uses it to evaluate new open-source projects without digging through folder structures; ByteGrad calls it a must-have for onboarding and PR review. Runs easily inside Docker.
connect_steps: 1) Generate a GitHub personal access token (repo scope). 2) Run the docker command above (or npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github). 3) Register the stdio/SSE server in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify repo/issue/PR tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Favorite AI MCP Servers for the Home Lab in 2026

name: Context7
purpose: Live, version-specific library documentation injected into agent prompts
description: Built by Upstash. Fetches current docs and code examples from official sources for tens of thousands of libraries (Next.js, React, Prisma, Supabase, Docker, Terraform, Python) so the agent codes against the real API instead of stale training data. Presenters in 3 of 5 videos (MaksDevInsights, VirtualizationHowto, BridgeMind, ByteGrad) recommend it as one of the first servers to install; supports CLAUDE.md rules/skills to auto-activate.
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp (optionally set CONTEXT7_API_KEY env var). 2) Register the stdio server in the MCP client config. 3) Restart the client; tools resolve-library-id and get-library-docs appear. 4) Optionally add a CLAUDE.md rule: 'use context7 for API docs'.
source: youtube:MCP Servers Every Developer Must Have in 2026

name: Supabase MCP
purpose: Live database schema, tables, migrations and SQL access inside the agent
description: Connects the agent to a live Supabase project: schema, relationships, foreign keys, list tables, run migrations, execute SQL, debug via logs. Presenter (MaksDevInsights) says the AI otherwise guesses at table structure; JeredBlu replaced his Postgres MCP server with it ('creates databases in a cinch'); ByteGrad notes it removes dashboard busywork. Setup via Supabase dashboard 'Connect > MCP' with per-client (Cursor/Claude Code/Codex) config and optional read-only permissions.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Supabase project and an access token (or use dashboard-generated MCP config). 2) Run the npx command with SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN and project ref env vars. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Authorize and verify schema/SQL tools are listed.
source: youtube:MCP Servers Every Developer Must Have in 2026

name: Figma MCP Server
purpose: Design-to-code: exposes live Figma layer structure, tokens and layout to the agent
description: Lets the coding agent generate code from a selected Figma frame, extract design context (variables, components, auto-layout values) - real hierarchy, not a screenshot. ByteGrad: OpenAI/Figma integration connects Claude Code/Codex directly to the design platform; MaksDevInsights wires it into Cursor so each Figma element carries a prompt the agent fetches and implements. Install via Figma plugin/desktop app or manual JSON config.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Figma personal access token (or install the official Figma MCP plugin). 2) Run the npx command with the token. 3) Register the stdio server in the MCP client config. 4) Open the Figma file and confirm frame/component tools appear.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code

name: shadcn/ui MCP Server
purpose: Browse and install shadcn/ui components from the registry via natural language
description: Allows AI assistants to interact with shadcn/ui registries: browse available components, search for specific ones, and install them directly into the project using natural language. ByteGrad converts a hard-coded dashboard into proper shadcn components ('convert this dashboard app into using proper shadcn components'); MaksDevInsights recommends it when there are no designs and you want to jump straight into implementation.
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y shadcn@latest mcp in the project. 2) Register the server in the MCP client config (project-level .mcp.json). 3) Restart client; tools get-project-registries / get-add-command-for-item appear.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code

name: Clerk MCP Server
purpose: Real user, org and session context for auth code generation
description: Lets the agent query actual user records, org memberships and session state so generated auth/OAuth code fits the real setup instead of a generic template. MaksDevInsights: 'your AI agent knows OAuth better than you do'; also helps avoid duplicated auth code. One-click setup or manual JSON config from the Clerk dashboard.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Clerk application and generate an MCP secret key. 2) Run: npx -y @clerk/mcp-server with CLERK_SECRET_KEY env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart and verify user/org/session tools are listed.
source: youtube:MCP Servers Every Developer Must Have in 2026

name: Sequential Thinking MCP
purpose: Forces structured chain-of-thought reasoning in any LLM client
description: Official reference server that forces the LLM to structure its thoughts step by step (comparable to Claude extended thinking / reasoning models). JeredBlu: 'I turn this on as much as I can. It takes a lot of tokens but makes every LLM a lot more powerful.'
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking. 2) Register the stdio server in the MCP client config. 3) Restart client and confirm the sequential-thinking tool is available.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Brave Search MCP
purpose: Web search grounding with a generous free tier
description: Grounds agent answers in real web data. JeredBlu: generous free tier, good at basic web data, also used inside Cursor and other MCP clients; notes Claude's native web search may be Brave-backed but the MCP works across all clients. ByteGrad lists it among web-access providers.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Brave Search API key (free tier). 2) Run: npx -y @brave/brave-search-mcp-server with BRAVE_API_KEY env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart and verify web-search tool is listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Tavily MCP
purpose: Deeper web search / research API for agents
description: Search API that goes a bit deeper than Brave Search, with a generous free tier. JeredBlu uses it alongside Brave and Firecrawl for grounding answers in real data.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Tavily API key (free tier). 2) Run: npx -y tavily-mcp with TAVILY_API_KEY env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart and verify search tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Firecrawl MCP
purpose: Web scraping and structured search results for agents
description: Web scraping + search API that returns structured results with snippets. JeredBlu: 'really good for web scraping'; ByteGrad notes it is quite popular, mostly for scraping but also plain search.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Firecrawl API key (free tier). 2) Run: npx -y firecrawl-mcp with FIRECRAWL_API_KEY env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart and verify scrape/search tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Notion MCP
purpose: Second brain: read/write tasks, notes and docs in Notion via the agent
description: Lets Claude/agent add to and pull from Notion: unified task list, product management, notes, PRDs, architecture docs, search. JeredBlu: 'essentially acts as my second brain'. ByteGrad highlights combining Notion MCP with design MCPs ('take the requirements document from Notion and create a design in Paper').
connect_steps: 1) Create a Notion integration and share the target pages/databases with it. 2) Run: npx -y @mcp-server-io/notion with NOTION_TOKEN env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart and verify page/database tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Desktop Commander MCP
purpose: Gives Claude/agent full computer control: read/write files, terminal, run code
description: Gives Claude the abilities of Cursor or Claude Code: read/write files, use the command line, modify the computer, code for you. JeredBlu: extremely powerful but potentially dangerous (like Cursor YOLO mode with even fewer guardrails - can change its own configs without asking); recommends running it on a separate user account. Config supports blocked commands, default shell, allowed directories (though terminal can still escape them).
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y @wshobson/agents (Desktop Commander mode). 2) Register in the MCP client config. 3) Restrict allowed directories/blocked commands in settings. 4) Restart client - use with caution and least privilege.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Taskmaster MCP
purpose: Turns PRDs into actionable task/subtask checklists and agent rules
description: Takes a product requirement document and breaks it into tasks and subtasks; creates Cursor rules, Windsurf rules and dev-workflow .mdc files. JeredBlu: prevents going in circles when vibe coding - the agent only starts the next task after completing the previous one; recommends adding rules to start a fresh chat every 2-3 tasks and run tests after each task.
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y taskmaster-ai. 2) Register in the MCP client config. 3) Point it at a PRD (product requirements doc). 4) Restart client and confirm task-planning tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Browser Tools MCP
purpose: Real-time Chrome DevTools console access for debugging web builds
description: Lets the agent see the Chrome developer console in real time while you build - instead of copy-pasting errors, it reads console output directly. JeredBlu: 'extremely useful for debugging... I use this all the time for anything I'm building that's web-based'. Requires the companion Chrome extension.
connect_steps: 1) Install the Browser Tools Chrome extension. 2) Run: npx -y @agentdesk/browser-tools-mcp. 3) Register the stdio server in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify console/network inspection tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: 21st.dev MCP (Magic)
purpose: AI-generated UI components and design elements
description: Design/UI generation server - creates polished UI elements and components for the agent. JeredBlu: 'the first MCP server I paid for, but it's really useful... really good for design and creating UI elements'.
connect_steps: 1) Create a 21st.dev account and API key. 2) Run: npx -y @21st-dev/magic-mcp with the API key. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify UI component tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Neo4j Aura MCP
purpose: Graph-database memory that persists across MCP clients
description: Knowledge-graph memory server on Neo4j Aura. JeredBlu switched from the standard memory MCP server to this one: 'a bit more flexible and it also works a lot better between the various MCP clients' - useful for long-term agent memory.
connect_steps: 1) Create a free Neo4j Aura instance and get connection credentials. 2) Run: uvx neo4j-mcp-server with NEO4J_URI/USER/PASSWORD env vars. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart and verify graph memory tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Pieces MCP Server
purpose: Shared memory across Claude, Gemini AI Studio, Perplexity and Cursor
description: Runs in the background, watches activity in Claude, Gemini AI Studio, Perplexity and Cursor, saves it to a database, and exposes it to the agent - a shared memory across all the LLMs you use. JeredBlu: powerful when switching between clients, but a privacy concern for companies (screen-watching).
connect_steps: 1) Install the Pieces desktop app and sign in. 2) Run: npx -y @pieces/app/mcp-server. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify context/recall tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Top 13 MCP Servers (That I Actually Use)

name: Proxmox MCP Server
purpose: Natural-language management and troubleshooting of Proxmox VE clusters
description: Exposes 200+ tools that talk to your Proxmox cluster through the official API: list running VMs, find nodes with most free memory, list stopped LXC containers, show snapshots, create a VM from a template, aggregate health stats across nodes. VirtualizationHowto's favorite: 'ask questions conversationally, manage and troubleshoot your Proxmox cluster'. Install by adding to your AI IDE (Cursor/VS Code).
connect_steps: 1) Create a Proxmox API token (PVE API user + token). 2) Run: uvx mcp-proxmox with PROXMOX_URL, PROXMOX_USER and token env vars. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify VM/container query tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Favorite AI MCP Servers for the Home Lab in 2026

name: Filesystem MCP Server
purpose: Understand entire directory structures instead of single files
description: Official reference server that lets AI understand a whole directory tree (not one file at a time) - great for Docker Compose projects with configs spread across folders, or re-orienting in projects you haven't touched in months. VirtualizationHowto: 'you explicitly choose which directories AI has permission to - least privilege instead of exposing your entire file system'.
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem <allowed-directory>. 2) Register in the MCP client config. 3) Restart client and verify file read/write/search tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Favorite AI MCP Servers for the Home Lab in 2026

name: Kubernetes MCP Server
purpose: Conversational kubectl: troubleshoot and learn Kubernetes via natural language
description: Wraps kubectl so you can ask 'why does this pod keep restarting?', 'which deployments are unhealthy?', 'which pods consume the most CPU?', 'which services expose node ports?', recent events in a namespace. VirtualizationHowto: 'dramatically reduces the time to understand what's happening inside your cluster' and flattens the learning curve for newcomers.
connect_steps: 1) Ensure a valid kubeconfig is available. 2) Run the docker command above (or npx -y @kubenet/kubernetes-mcp-server). 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify pod/deployment/event query tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Favorite AI MCP Servers for the Home Lab in 2026

name: jcodemunch MCP (jcodec)
purpose: Indexes your codebase so the agent stops re-grepping everything (cuts token spend)
description: Creates an index of your project and understands how everything is connected, so the AI finds functions, config files and docs without repeatedly searching the whole codebase. VirtualizationHowto: searching/grepping large codebases is one of the biggest consumers of cloud AI credits - this dramatically reduces token consumption and speeds up responses, and the tool even shows tokens/money saved. Part of a family with jdocmunch (docs) and jdatamunch (data).
connect_steps: 1) Install the jcodemunch MCP server (see jcodec project docs; runs as a local server). 2) Point it at your project root. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify index/search tools are listed.
source: youtube:My Favorite AI MCP Servers for the Home Lab in 2026

name: PostHog MCP
purpose: Autonomous product analytics: agent reads traffic/funnel data and improves conversions
description: Gives the agent access to PostHog analytics (traffic sources, conversion funnels, page drop-off) and lets it cross-reference that data with your code to build structured conversion-optimization plans. BridgeMind: 'if you have a website or an app, you should be using this MCP' - used daily to review analytics and drive conversion fixes in Cursor plan mode.
connect_steps: 1) Create a PostHog project and personal API key. 2) Run: uvx posthog-mcp with POSTHOG_API_KEY and POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID env vars. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify analytics query tools are listed.
source: youtube:Top 5 MCP Servers For Vibe Coding In 2026

name: Sentry MCP Server
purpose: Real-time error tracking: agent reads production errors and plans fixes
description: Connects the agent to Sentry so it can review production errors/issues (500s, 400s, browser info, events), search issues and cross-reference them with the local codebase to create structured fix plans. BridgeMind: 13 tools enabled (whoami, find organizations/teams/projects/releases, get issue details, search issues/events) - 'definitely an MCP server you want integrated into your daily vibe coding workflow'.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Sentry auth token (org:read, project:read scopes). 2) Run: uvx sentry-mcp with SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN and SENTRY_ORG env vars. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify issue/event search tools are listed.
source: youtube:Top 5 MCP Servers For Vibe Coding In 2026

name: BridgeMind MCP
purpose: Agent task orchestration: create tasks with instructions+knowledge on a Kanban board for sub-agents
description: Lets a parent agent create tasks (each carrying a system-prompt-style instruction block plus knowledge/context) on a BridgeMind Kanban board and pass them to sub-agents with fresh context windows - solving the context-window hallucination problem in agent swarms. BridgeMind: 49 tools, 4 prompts, 4 resources; used to run parallel security audits that spawn fix tasks. Paid (Pro plan, 7-day trial; 50% off at launch).
connect_steps: 1) Create a BridgeMind account (bridgemind.ai) and project. 2) Follow the MCP setup instructions in the BridgeMind dashboard to get the server config/API key. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify task/kanban tools are listed.
source: youtube:Top 5 MCP Servers For Vibe Coding In 2026

name: Exa MCP
purpose: Ultra-powerful real-time web + code search (better than built-in web search)
description: Advanced web search with full control over filters, domains, dates and content options (web-search-advanced tool). BridgeMind: 'better than your out of the box web search from Claude, Cursor or Codex... completely free, very powerful' - used to verify a Stripe integration against current 2026 docs. Connects Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code and 10+ AI assistants.
connect_steps: 1) Create an Exa API key (free tier). 2) Run: npx -y exa-mcp-server with EXA_API_KEY env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify search tools (web-search-advanced) are listed.
source: youtube:Top 5 MCP Servers For Vibe Coding In 2026

name: Paper MCP
purpose: Agent-driven infinite canvas: design in a desktop canvas, implement back in code
description: Desktop canvas app with powerful MCP capabilities: the agent can bring a live code app into the Paper canvas (writes HTML/CSS to draw), create layout variations, then implement the new design back into code. ByteGrad: 'went viral, a lot of people use it with Claude Code... really interesting workflow - bring designs and code back and forth'. Requires the Paper desktop application; local MCP server.
connect_steps: 1) Install the Paper desktop application and sign in. 2) Add the Paper MCP server to the client (per the Paper docs command). 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify canvas tools (create artboard, write HTML) are listed.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code

name: Pencil MCP
purpose: Infinite design canvas inside your IDE, driven by the agent
description: Installed as an IDE extension, it gives you a canvas inside your editor (no app switching): create .pen files and prompt the agent to edit frames ('turn the step one frame into dark mode', 'add three more rows'). ByteGrad: 'very tight feedback cycle because you don't have to switch between different apps... a lot of the design features you expect on an infinite canvas'.
connect_steps: 1) Install the Pencil IDE extension (VS Code / Cursor). 2) Create a .pen file to activate the canvas. 3) Restart the client so the Pencil MCP is picked up. 4) Verify canvas/frame tools are listed in the MCP menu.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code

name: Playwright MCP
purpose: Browser automation and smoke testing via the agent (fill forms, click, screenshot, console)
description: Gives the coding agent browser automation: navigate to URLs, fill/submit forms, click elements, drag, hover, take screenshots, read console messages and list network requests. ByteGrad: 'if you want to test a user flow or reproduce a bug someone is reporting, or give your agent easy access to console errors, this is a great MCP server'. Opens its own browser window (does not reuse your session).
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y @playwright/mcp@latest. 2) Register the stdio server in the MCP client config. 3) Restart client and verify browser tools (navigate, click, screenshot, console) are listed.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code

name: Chrome DevTools MCP
purpose: Debug a live browser session: network, performance traces, elements (reuses your logged-in session)
description: Lets the agent access your real (signed-in) browser session: analyze network requests, record performance traces and extract insights, take screenshots, automate via Puppeteer under the hood. ByteGrad highlights the significant update: 'reuse an existing browser session' - the agent can debug issues gated behind sign-in and investigate failing network requests directly from the Network panel. Autoconnect mode reuses your open Chrome window (remote debugging must be enabled).
connect_steps: 1) Run: npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest. 2) Register in the MCP client config. 3) For session reuse, launch Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9222 and use autoconnect mode. 4) Restart client and verify trace/network/screenshot tools are listed.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code

name: Vercel MCP
purpose: Deployment analysis: agent inspects projects, deployments and logs, fixes failures
description: Gives the agent access to Vercel projects and deployments to analyze deployment logs and fix failing deploys ('analyze why the deployment failed and fix the issues'). ByteGrad: makes first deployments much smoother because the agent has access to the errors and failure reasons; also host your own MCP servers on Vercel via the TypeScript SDK.
connect_steps: 1) Create a Vercel access token. 2) Run: npx -y @vercel/mcp-server with VERCEL_TOKEN env var. 3) Register in the MCP client config. 4) Restart client and verify deployment/project tools are listed.
source: youtube:Top 11 MCP-Servers for Claude Code
